subject: Customer ask: carve-out impact on tenant logging & retention (SOC 2)
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@aureus-data.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick clarification: SOC2 carve-out for cloud logging/retention

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the SOC2 report you shared earlier. Our compliance team reviewed Redwood's 2026 SOC 2 Type II and has one open item: the report states that cloud logging (GCP Stackdriver / BigQuery & Azure Monitor) is operated by the cloud provider and appears to be scoped as a carve-out/subservice. We need to confirm how that carve-out affects audit evidence for tenant-level audit logs and retention for our account.

Specifically: 
- Will Redwood provide tenant-level logging (access, admin-change, and config) within our account for the audit period (Jan 1 2026 - Dec 31 2026), or should we rely on the cloud provider's SOC?
- If cloud provider coverage is used, can Redwood provide a bridge letter or subservice attestation explaining responsibility split (who is responsible for retention/retrieval during the audit window)?

We have an upcoming audit kickoff on July 12 and need clarity by July 2 to include in the control narrative. Attaching our SIG/Qs.

Best,
Elena Ortiz
Security Operations Manager
Aureus DataWorks

Attachments: Aureus-SIG-questions.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@aureus-data.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick clarification: SOC2 carve-out for cloud logging/retention

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear questions and the SIG. Quick summary up front: Redwood's hosted control plane is in-scope for SOC 2, but we rely on cloud providers for hypervisor/physical and certain managed logging services. That means: 

- Application-level tenant logs (access events from Redwood app, API keys use, admin-change events captured by our service) are retained by Redwood and are available as evidence for the audit window.
- Provider-managed infrastructure logs (host OS, underlying cloud-managed monitor service control plane logs) are scoped to the cloud provider's report and are typically carve-outs.

Marissa, can you confirm the retention windows we retained for tenant-level audit logs during 2026 and whether we can provide an export for Aureus's tenant? Karthik — please confirm whether any of the tenant-level logging we capture relied on a cloud-managed collector that would create a dependence on provider evidence.

I can provide a short attestation/cover note and ask our compliance team to draft a bridge letter if needed. Targeting to get a response by 6/30 so you can include in your kickoff.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@aureus-data.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick clarification: SOC2 carve-out for cloud logging/retention

Hi all —

Looping in Compliance / Evidence. Short answers: 

- Tenant-level application logs for Aureus (API access, admin-change events, workspace activity) were retained within Redwood's logging pipeline. Our retention policy in 2026 for security audit logs was 18 months by default for paid accounts; for the audited period (2026 calendar year) those logs exist and we can generate exports scoped to Aureus's tenant id.

- For infrastructure/cloud-provider logs (e.g., GCP control plane events), Redwood relied on the provider's SOC as subservice evidence. Those remain carve-outs and we cannot produce underlying provider-managed audit control logs.

Action: I will prepare a one-page attestation that: (a) enumerates what types of logs Redwood retained and can export, (b) confirms retention windows, and (c) references the providers and notes the provider-SOC carve-out. If Aureus needs a formal bridge letter referencing Redwood's reliance on provider SOC reports, we will generate that and propose signatures.

I'll attach the export template so Elena knows the CSV fields.

-Marissa
Director, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-log-export-template.csv, Redwood-2026-SOC2-TypeII-summary-stub.pdf
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@aureus-data.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick clarification: SOC2 carve-out for cloud logging/retention

Thanks Marissa — that's helpful. Two quick clarifying Qs from our auditor: 
1) For the tenant-level logs you can export, can you confirm the earliest and latest timestamp fields included and whether the export includes the actor identity (user id or service account) and IP address?
2) If we accept a bridge letter referencing provider SOCs for the cloud-managed logs, will Redwood accept responsibility to facilitate retrieval requests from our auditors to the provider? Our auditors often request provider artifacts during testing.

If we can get the export template and attestation by 6/30, we can mark the item as covered in our control narrative.

-Elena
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@aureus-data.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:24:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick clarification: SOC2 carve-out for cloud logging/retention

Elena —

Answers below and next steps: 

1) Export contents: the tenant export includes the following fields: event_timestamp (UTC), tenant_id, user_id, actor_type (user/service), event_type, resource, ip_address, request_id, raw_event_json. The earliest event for 2026 is 2026-01-01T00:00:03Z and the latest is 2026-12-31T23:59:58Z for your workspace.

2) Bridge letter & auditor facilitation: Redwood will provide a bridge letter that documents the shared responsibility model and lists provider SOC reports relied on. While we are not the authority on provider artifacts, we will coordinate with the auditor to request provider evidence on your behalf where required (e.g., raise the retrieval request and provide the provider SOC references). We cannot guarantee provider cooperation or timeline, and that will be noted in the bridge letter.

Deliverables by 6/30 (attached): 
- One-page attestation/one-paragraph cover note (Redwood-attestation-aureus-6-30-2027.pdf)
- Log export template (redwood-log-export-template.csv)
- Draft bridge letter (Redwood-bridgeletter-template.docx)

Please confirm if you want us to proceed to formalize the bridge letter and route to signatures (DocuSign).

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: Redwood-attestation-aureus-6-30-2027.pdf, Redwood-bridgeletter-template.docx, redwood-log-export-template.csv
